requirement: Hold the MPS processing-service eligibility certificate if the service falls within the regulated category.
how: Software capabilities cannot establish the supplier’s licence or its approved service scope.
gap: Obtain certificate, issue date and scope; Vietnamese counsel must confirm SaaS/support applicability before a contractual claim.
app: No application feature can issue or replace the supplier certificate. Technical findings below support the application dossier.
manual: Identify the applicant legal entity and obtain a Vietnamese scope opinion; follow the MPS steps below. Apply in the organisation’s name, for the actual services offered.
evidence: Applicability opinion; submitted Form 04 and dossier; application receipt; issued certificate and approved scope. Until issued, certificate evidence is pending.

requirement: Vietnamese incorporation, eligible resident head of processing and at least three qualified staff.
how: These are company and staffing obligations rather than application features.
gap: Provide registration, appointment, citizenship/residence evidence and qualifications. Confirm that this licensing category applies.
app: No code fix for incorporation, citizenship, residence or professional qualifications.
manual: Provide Vietnamese registration; appoint the eligible professional head; employ at least three qualified privacy staff and document management competence. Validate qualifications against Article 13(2).
evidence: Registration; head appointment/citizenship/permanent-residence proof; three personnel files with education, experience, training, confidentiality agreements and duties.

requirement: Obtain a satisfactory supplier processing impact-assessment result, plus a cross-border assessment result where transfers occur.
law: ND356 Art 22(4); PDPL assessment rules; OB_J_005 [M1]
how: Actual data inventory and controls support preparation; no satisfactory regulatory assessment result was established. A filing receipt alone does not meet this eligibility condition. [E1–E10]
dates:
1 Jan 2026
Filing clock depends on processing commencement [L5,L6]
gap: Produce supplier dossier and submission receipt. Record the first-processing date and distinguish filing from regulatory approval.
app: No statutory requirement for an in-app filing screen. Engineering must supply the actual data inventory, access model and flows for the assessment.
manual: Prepare the supplier assessment and obtain the satisfactory assessment result required by Article 22(4); mere filing receipt is insufficient. Assess cross-border processing as well when present.
evidence: Supplier processing assessment; submission receipt and satisfactory result; cross-border assessment/result where applicable; versioned data-flow annex.

requirement: Demonstrate infrastructure, equipment, facilities and technology appropriate to the processing service.
how: Encryption, tenancy, backup and access controls exist, but whole-estate security and suitability are not yet evidenced. [E3,E5,E8]
dates:
1 Jan 2026
Before application eligibility is asserted [M1]
app: Close the scoped security, data-flow, access, backup and audit findings in A03/A04/A12/A14; test the real infrastructure supporting the declared service.
manual: Document asset/facility ownership or contracts, architecture, staff competence and security suitability.
evidence: Infrastructure asset register/contracts; architecture; scoped security/restore/isolation tests; documented suitability assessment.

requirement: Maintain periodic compliance evaluation and required organisation identity authentication.
how: Release records exist; no annual compliance evaluation or compliant organisation-identity verification evidence was established. [E9]
dates:
1 Jan 2026
Annual evaluation; identity duty ongoing [M1]
app: Verify the existing entity-authentication workflow; add provider integration only if the approved method cannot be completed and evidenced outside the app.
manual: Perform the required entity authentication; schedule annual compliance evaluation; retain risk framework, responsibilities and findings/actions.
evidence: Organisation-authentication evidence; annual evaluation plan/report; risk register, responsibility policy and follow-up actions.

requirement: Sign a data-processing agreement before receiving clinic data; define roles and purposes.
law: PDPL processor duties; ND356 Art 12; OB_J_006–011
how: Consent and access controls support agreed processing, but do not prove a signed agreement exists. [E1,E5]
gap: Provide executed DPA, Vietnamese protection clause, role allocation, support scope and permitted purposes. Counsel to confirm the draft’s unspecified PDPL article.
app: No code fix to create legal agreement validity. Use existing controls only after the agreement and actual purposes align.
manual: Sign the DPA before receiving data. Define clinic/supplier roles, scope, protection duties, confidentiality and subprocessors.
evidence: Executed dated DPA; permitted-purpose schedule; contract review/signatory authority; onboarding gate record.

requirement: Control support, analytics, AI use and model training within the agreed purposes.
how: Consent types and scope notes exist. AI coding and speech processing have consent checks and cloud gates; an AI egress guard covers selected callers. [E1,E7]
gap: Approve a purpose register and no-training terms; review every AI caller. AI guard coverage and a provider named Ollama do not establish location or purpose compliance.
app: A01/A12: enforce purpose-specific checks for support, AI, analytics and training; cover every outbound caller. Generic data_sharing must not substitute for an approved specific purpose.
manual: Approve purpose/legal-basis inventory; restrict model training and secondary use contractually; assess vendors and minimise payloads.
evidence: Purpose-to-feature map; contract terms; deny/allow tests for each purpose and endpoint; redacted egress logs; provider retention/no-training terms.

requirement: Identify sub-processors and notify material data-flow and hosting changes.
how: Git history and rollout tools identify software versions; they are not an approved sub-processor register or client notification record. [E9]
gap: List hosting, backups, AI, email, calling and support vendors, countries and functions; agree change notice and approvals.
app: No mandatory bespoke register screen. Existing release tracking can supply changes; add workflow tooling only if notices cannot be reliably evidenced.
manual: Maintain the processor list with function, country, data and access; agree notice and approval rules; send and retain material-change notices.
evidence: Approved subprocessor register; data-flow diagram; vendor contracts; dated notification/approval records.

requirement: Return/export data at exit and define deletion and ongoing custody.
how: FHIR patient export and database-plus-filestore backup are implemented. Closing a tenant takes a final backup first. [E6,E8]
gap: Agree complete export format, attachments and metadata, handover timetable, archive custodian and deletion certificate. Final backups are retained indefinitely by default.
app: A05/A06: export full records, attachments, addenda, consent and audit metadata; guard tenant shutdown against retention/legal holds; replace unlimited backup retention with approved rules.
manual: Agree handover format, timetable, custody and lawful deletion; assign the receiving custodian and rehearse exit.
evidence: Sample export manifest/checksums and receiving-side read test; signed exit clause; custody acceptance; scoped deletion or retained-data certificate.

requirement: Store tenant personal data and user-created data in Vietnam under the client’s proposed hosting requirement.
how: Live instance metadata reports ap-southeast-2, the Sydney region. The configured platform therefore fails the document’s Vietnam-only assumption. [E10]
gap: Confirm the clinic’s actual hosting scope and legal applicability; plan Vietnam hosting for database, attachments, logs, replicas and backups. No migration was performed.
app: Infrastructure change required: establish a Vietnam deployment covering DB, filestore, logs, replicas, backups and relevant AI services; update endpoint/routing configuration and verify regional isolation.
manual: Select and contract the Vietnam provider; approve migration, restore validation and transfer treatment with counsel. The observed Sydney host does not meet the client’s Vietnam-only condition.
evidence: Hosting contract and actual region evidence for each component; deployment/data-flow diagram; approved migration plan and post-migration verification.

requirement: Assess foreign access and cross-border processing, including support, backups and AI.
how: Scribe and AI coding allow_cloud flags are False on master, hhh and template. Time-limited support sessions are recorded. These controls do not prove Vietnam residency. [E7,E8,E10]
gap: Map every transfer/access path and recipient. Complete required transfer dossiers; counsel must assess exemptions and important/core-data thresholds rather than treating all access identically.
app: A12: validate actual destination/location and block unapproved data egress; a provider type or private IP is not sufficient proof. Audit support and third-party paths.
manual: Inventory all remote access/transfers, processors and destinations; obtain required transfer assessment/result and contracts; approve narrow documented exceptions.
evidence: Transfer register and applicable dossier/result; support approvals; endpoint allowlist; blocked-destination tests; provider-region evidence.

requirement: Encrypt patient data at rest and in transit, with controlled key custody.
how: AES-256-GCM protects selected identifiers and note narratives. HTTPS certificates are described in the runbook. Encryption module is installed in reviewed active systems. [E3,E8,E10]
gap: Verify live TLS, database/disks, attachments, audio, logs and backups. Backup code compresses but does not itself encrypt. Confirm external key custody, rotation and old plaintext migration.
app: A04: encrypt backup artifacts and uncovered sensitive attachments/audio; verify legacy migration; enforce external key custody and rotation. Infrastructure must supply TLS and disk/storage protection.
manual: Assign key custodians; approve access, rotation, recovery and encryption standards. Validate the whole storage estate rather than selected fields only.
evidence: Encryption inventory; redacted key-storage/rotation proof; TLS report; migration counts; encrypted backup and successful controlled decrypt/restore test.

requirement: Separate clients’ application data, storage and applicable network security zones.
how: Platform provisions a database and filestore per tenant and routes by hostname. Application servers and host infrastructure are shared. [E8,E10]
gap: Document database/filestore permissions and network zones. Test cross-tenant access and restore isolation; determine the required security level.
app: No new isolation code is established as necessary yet. Test database, filestore, API, browser and restore boundaries; fix failures and implement required network zoning.
manual: Determine security classification; document shared-host risks, DB permissions and network isolation; approve the boundary design.
evidence: Cross-tenant negative-test results; permission/network diagram; storage isolation report; classification decision.

requirement: Capture required security events and retain investigation-ready logs for at least 12 months where applicable.
how: API audit stores user, timestamp, IP, method, route and touched subjects; application write/delete guards make those rows append-only. [E4]
gap: Combine application, authentication and proxy logs. API model has no source-port or login/logout fields and no evidenced 12-month retention/immutable archive policy.
app: A03: add missing authentication and clinical event coverage; capture source port in the correct proxy/network layer; route to protected log storage with at least the applicable retention period.
manual: Define log specification, lawful access, retention, retrieval and privileged monitoring; provision a separately protected archive.
evidence: Sample login/logout/access/change/delete/proxy events; accurate actor/IP/source port; retention configuration; immutable archive and retrieval/tamper tests.

requirement: Respond to lawful MPS requests within the applicable 24-hour period.
how: Exportable records and API audit data provide technical inputs, but no request-response process or staffed SLA is established. [E4,E6]
dates:
1 Jul 2026
24 hours where request rule applies [L11]
gap: Counsel confirms scope and trigger; name an on-call owner, verify authority and preserve disclosure records. Rehearse a timed response.
app: Existing exports can support responses. No mandatory new request portal; add reporting only if a timed rehearsal shows extraction gaps.
manual: Appoint an on-call responder; validate lawful requests with counsel; preserve records and meet the applicable clock.
evidence: Request handling procedure; contacts; mock lawful-request receipt, extraction and response timestamps; authorised disclosure log.

requirement: Handle breaches and notify the clinic early enough for its authority-reporting obligations.
how: Audit components support investigation; no completed incident plan, notification SLA or rehearsal establishes readiness. [E4]
gap: Confirm statutory reportability/clock; agree immediate escalation and a shorter supplier-to-clinic SLA. Produce contacts, incident procedure and tabletop evidence.
app: No mandatory application incident module. Verify detection/alerts and log completeness; fix those controls under A03 as needed.
manual: Approve an incident plan, supplier-to-clinic escalation SLA and reportability rules; train staff; run a timed tabletop and retain evidence.
evidence: Signed incident plan/contact tree; alert example; tabletop report; notification template, deadlines and receipt logs.

requirement: Provide technical evidence for the clinic’s security-level dossier and risk assessment.
how: Architecture, permissions, encryption and tenancy documentation are available inputs. [E3,E5,E8]
gap: Prepare system boundary, classification, controls, network diagram, penetration-test report and dossier sections for independent review.
app: Provide technical diagrams, controls and test results from the remedied release; no application feature can approve a security-level dossier.
manual: Classify the system; assemble the dossier, commission penetration testing, remediate material findings and obtain the required review/approval.
evidence: System boundary and classification; control matrix; penetration-test/remediation report; dossier and applicable approval/acceptance.

requirement: Evidence any claimed ISO 27001 or voluntarily adopted international standard.
law: OB_IS_E; ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST by choice
how: Application controls alone do not prove an independently certified management system.
dates:
No Vietnamese commencement date
Voluntary or contractual
gap: Provide valid certificate with scope and issuer if claimed; otherwise record the adopted controls and verification basis without claiming certification.
app: No code fix establishes ISO certification. Reuse relevant technical evidence; close actual certification-audit findings if the standard is adopted.
manual: Confirm whether certification is contractual; obtain an accredited certificate in scope if claimed, or describe adopted controls without a certification claim.
evidence: Valid certificate, scope and verification if claimed; otherwise signed standards/adopted-control register and independent review.

requirement: Associate notes with an authenticated author and recorded time; distinguish care time from entry time.
how: Notes default author_id to the logged-in user and carry create_date. Finalization captures signer, role and signed_datetime; notes link to a service visit. [E2]
gap: Demonstrate real care-time capture, offline entry reconciliation and individual accounts. Protect author_id/order_id on finalized notes; neither is in EMR_LOCKED_FIELDS.
app: A02: lock finalized author_id and order_id; capture care/event time separately from entry/signing time; validate offline attribution and individual authenticated authors.
manual: Approve contemporaneous-recording, late-entry and offline reconciliation procedures; train clinicians; forbid shared accounts.
evidence: Test notes with distinct care/entry/sign times; identity/relink mutation denial; offline sync tests; late-entry policy and training record.

requirement: Preserve finalized content and prevent silent overwriting or deletion through ordinary application operations.
how: Finalized narrative, ciphertext and seal fields are locked; notes cannot be unlinked, and deleting a visit with finalized notes is blocked. SHA-256 verification detects changed sealed content. [E2]
gap: Confirm deployed behavior with a witnessed test. Database/host administrator changes are outside the ORM guard; protect and monitor privileged access.
app: Keep existing final-content and visit-deletion guards. Run mutation/cascade and privileged-access tests; fix any bypass found. A02 closes identity fields separately.
manual: Restrict and monitor DB/host administrators; approve clinical finalization policy and tamper response.
evidence: Witnessed final-content mutation/deletion/cascade tests; integrity check result; privileged-access controls and alert test.

requirement: Corrections preserve original content, correction author, time and reason.
how: Addenda link to a finalized same-patient note via amends_note_id. Original finalized content remains locked. New records have author/time metadata. [E2]
gap: Make a correction reason mandatory and export original/addendum history together. Demonstrate author, timestamps and reason; no dedicated required reason field was identified.
app: A02: require a correction reason; preserve original/addendum identity, timestamps and link; include the complete correction chain in exports.
manual: Approve addendum/late-correction policy and clinical reviewer workflow.
evidence: Original and addendum example with mandatory reason; empty-reason refusal; original unchanged checksum; exported correction chain.

requirement: Audit viewing, creation, change and deletion of each clinical record; protect against alteration.
law: LGDDT; OB_IS_G is voluntary; source topic 05
how: API/FHIR access audit and clinical finalization chatter exist. The consolidated healthcare audit SQL view excludes health.clinical.note and records tracked changes only. [E2,E4]
dates:
1 Jul 2024
Voluntary practice has no local start date [L7]
gap: Cover backend/PWA reads and all record events, correct actor mapping, and preserve logs independently of DB administrators. Demonstrate audit export and privileged-access monitoring.
app: A03: cover backend/PWA reads and all create/change/delete events; include clinical notes in reporting; correct partner/user actor mapping; protect logs beyond ORM guards.
manual: Assign audit reviewers and privileged-access responsibilities; agree evidence retention and regular review.
evidence: Full clinical event sequence across API/backend/PWA; correct actor mapping; exported trail; protected-store tamper detection and reviewer sign-off.

requirement: Restrict clinical access by role and revoke permissions when required.
how: Nurse, doctor and owner ACLs plus catchment rules constrain notes. Finalization is restricted to author or head nurse; user/role administration supports grant and revocation. [E2,E5]
gap: Provide a client-approved permission matrix and witnessed grant/revoke tests, including exports, sessions and emergency access. Yes applies to implemented controls, not all deployed assignments.
app: Verify existing ACL/catchment controls and immediate session/API revocation. No new role model is required unless tests expose a bypass.
manual: Approve least-privilege role matrix; provision/revoke personal accounts; periodically recertify privileged access.
evidence: Signed role matrix; role/catchment denial tests; grant/revoke/session tests; user access review.

requirement: Apply record-class retention of 10, 20, 30 years or permanent preservation as appropriate.
how: Finalized notes are protected from application deletion; records can be archived. There is no evidenced record-class retention clock or legal-hold engine. [E2,E8]
gap: Adopt a class-based schedule. Ordinary inpatient/outpatient records: 10 years; specified classes: 20; death medical records: 30; incident-resolution dossiers: permanent. Protect exit and purge flows.
app: A05: add record-class retention, legal holds, controlled disposal and protected exit/decommissioning; cover related attachments and backups.
manual: Custodian approves the class schedule and clock triggers, medical/incident classes, holds and disposal authority.
evidence: Approved schedule; per-class expiry/hold tests; refusal to purge retained records/whole tenant; disposal approvals.

requirement: Keep archives readable and retrievable with metadata throughout the required period and after service exit.
law: LGDDT Art 13; TT33; conditional LLT; OB_G_005–006
how: FHIR JSON export and paired database/filestore backups preserve useful content; restore-to-staging capability exists. [E6,E8]
gap: Specify long-term formats, schemas, checksums, keys, attachments, periodic migration and retrieval tests; contractually assign ongoing archive custody. Fourteen nightly backups are not a medical retention schedule.
app: A06/A14: export durable formats with schemas, metadata, attachments and checksums; validate archive retrieval and migrations; preserve keys.
manual: Contract archive custody after exit; set migration/retrieval checks and storage service obligations.
evidence: Archive manifest; schema/format list; migrated sample readability; retrieval test; custody agreement and long-term key plan.

requirement: Delete personal data securely when deletion is lawful, including governed handling of backup copies.
how: Soft delete and archive retain the record. Owner purge can remove ordinary records; tenant closure retains a final backup indefinitely. These are not verified secure erasure. [E8]
gap: Add lawful-deletion review, legal-hold checks, backup expiry/crypto-erasure and deletion certificates. Prevent restoration of deleted data into active processing.
app: A05: distinguish soft delete from lawful erasure; implement hold-aware purge, backup expiry/crypto-erasure, tombstones and prevention of reintroducing deleted data.
manual: DPO/custodian authorises deletion or lawful refusal; approve backup handling and certificate wording.
evidence: Live-data erasure test; attachment removal; backup expiry/crypto-erasure evidence; restore suppression test; signed deletion/retention certificate.

requirement: Track and answer deletion requests within the applicable response periods.
how: No dedicated verified data-subject request workflow with statutory timers, refusal grounds and completed-erasure evidence was identified.
gap: Confirm exact acknowledgement, completion and extension rules with counsel. Implement identity verification, deadline tracking and documented refusal where medical retention overrides deletion.
app: A07: add a reliable rights-request case record with identity checks, statutory clocks, lawful refusal/extensions, processor handoff and completion evidence. An integrated case tool may satisfy this without duplicating a module.
manual: Appoint case owner; approve identity/refusal/extension procedures and vendor response SLAs.
evidence: Request/acknowledgement/fulfilment timestamps; 20/30-day deletion workflow, legal-retention refusal and justified extension tests; closed sample case.

requirement: Capture positive consent separately by purpose, method and evidence.
how: health.consent stores consent type, scope, verbal witness or written/drawn evidence, effective/expiry dates and explicit grant state. Evidence fields lock after draft. [E1]
gap: Approve notices and lawful bases per purpose, ensure meaningful choice and classify representative consent. A drawn image called digital_signature is not a CA digital signature.
app: A01: retain notice version and exact affirmative grant time; map each purpose to its enforcement paths and representative authority. Keep existing capture/evidence locks.
manual: Approve each purpose’s notice/legal basis and representative rules; obtain valid consent before consent-dependent processing.
evidence: Printable consent with subject/grantor, purpose, notice version, evidence and grant time; representative validation and no-silence grant test.

requirement: Produce consent evidence in printable form and retain it throughout processing.
how: Written evidence attachments, consent metadata and FHIR Consent serialization are available. Active consent evidence has application locks. [E1,E6]
gap: Provide a complete printable consent record including notice/version, purpose, grantor, evidence, dates and withdrawal history; verify retention and attachment readability. No dedicated print report was identified.
app: A01: produce a complete printable consent record and immutable history, including grant/withdrawal timestamps, evidence and notice text/version.
manual: Approve retention of consent evidence for the processing period and valid access to the evidence.
evidence: Readable consent PDF/HTML sample; attached evidence; withdrawal history; retention test and custodian approval.

requirement: Record consent withdrawal and stop processing that relies on the withdrawn purpose.
how: Withdrawal records date, actor and reason; subsequent checks deny withdrawn consent. Generic require_consent defaults to log-only. FHIR flag is True on master but False on hhh and template. [E1,E6,E10]
dates:
1 Jan 2026
At withdrawal, subject to lawful exceptions [L5]
gap: Enforce relevant gates per tenant and purpose, test queued jobs/offline caches and marketing/exports. Date-only withdrawal metadata needs an exact time for immediate-stop evidence.
app: A01/A12: enable the correct flags per tenant/template and enforce all relevant paths; record exact withdrawal time; stop queued/new consent-dependent work and reconcile offline caches.
manual: Approve exceptions/ongoing lawful retention; tell staff and vendors which purpose must stop; review tenant settings after cloning.
evidence: Before/after-withdrawal tests across FHIR/backend/PWA/AI/marketing/queue; config inventory for every in-scope DB; preserved lawful records; time-stamped withdrawal.

requirement: Provide patient access, copies and an understandable record summary on request.
how: FHIR Patient/$everything and Vietnam bundle export assemble patient-linked clinical resources. Portal provides patient-facing history. [E6]
gap: Verify completeness, attachments and addenda; provide a readable clinical summary and request workflow with identity and representative checks. JSON export alone is not a patient-readable summary.
app: A06/A07: provide complete readable copies/summary with attachments/addenda and request tracking. Verify FHIR completeness against the record inventory.
manual: Custodian verifies identity and representative authority; provides the copy/summary under the approved workflow.
evidence: Reconciled sample record versus export; readable summary and attachments; authority check; request, fulfilment and receipt timestamps.

requirement: Provide the lawful signing or confirmation method required for each clinical document.
how: Clinician finalization records identity and a content hash. signature_ref is reserved for future CA integration; drawn consent signature evidence is an image. [E1,E2]
gap: Select and validate a lawful method by document and intended use. TT13 allows lawful electronic signatures, biometrics or other lawful confirmation; current finalization is not proved legally equivalent to handwriting.
app: Select the lawful method first. Existing login/finalization/hash is not proved sufficient. Implement A08 when the selected method needs certified signing or stronger confirmation.
manual: Clinical/legal team specifies permissible method by document, handwritten-equivalence requirements and provider contracts.
evidence: Method-by-document opinion; authentication/signing design; witnessed confirmation/signing test; provider eligibility evidence if used.

requirement: When using CA digital signing, check certificates and detect altered signed content.
how: Hash verification is implemented; no CA signing transaction, stored certificate-status proof or externally verifiable signed document was identified. [E2]
gap: Integrate an eligible provider; retain certificate chain/status at signing, signed bytes and verification result. Demonstrate invalidation and independent verification on a sample.
app: A08: integrate eligible CA signing where required; store signed bytes/certificate chain/status at signing; expose verification and tamper invalidation.
manual: Select provider and protect signer credentials; agree verification and long-term signature preservation.
evidence: Externally verified signed sample; status/chain proof; altered-content invalidation; expiry/revocation scenarios; signer/key custody record.

requirement: Meet the applicable transition for integrated signing and signature-verification software.
how: The reserved signature field is an integration anchor, not a conforming signing or verification component. [E2]
gap: Validate the cited two-year transition and current technical rules with counsel/provider; deliver a conforming integration before its applicable deadline. The transition does not postpone existing record duties.
app: A08: deliver/test the applicable signing and verification component requirements, including current technical standards. A placeholder signature_ref is not completion.
manual: Confirm current transition scope with counsel/provider; schedule before the applicable 10 April 2027 deadline from the client source.
evidence: Component version and conformance matrix; independent verification report; provider confirmation of applicable transition/current rules.

requirement: Back up EMR and attachments to separate storage and demonstrate restoration.
how: Tenant backup code captures PostgreSQL plus filestore, checks sizes and restores to staging with jobs disabled. Runbook retains 14 nightly copies. [E8]
gap: Prove separate failure-domain storage in Vietnam, encryption, RPO/RTO, scheduled success and a dated restore test. Current code writes local backup paths; storage independence is not established.
app: A04/A14: provide encrypted paired backups to an independent failure domain; verify restore, keys, attachments and jobs-off behavior. Local paths alone are insufficient.
manual: Provision approved Vietnam storage; assign RPO/RTO and schedules; rehearse restores and review failed-backup alerts.
evidence: Successful dated restore report with DB/attachment reconciliation; backup schedule/region/failure-domain proof; encryption/keys; measured RPO/RTO.

requirement: Link records to the patient personal identification number and validate identifiers.
how: Encrypted national_id/CCCD fields are serialized into FHIR. Vietnam validation flags missing identifiers, but errors do not block export; VNeID verified flag is manual. [E3,E6]
gap: Require and validate identity under applicable patient rules; resolve duplicates and exceptions. Demonstrate patient linkage and authoritative verification. Manual VNeID confirmation is not an integration.
app: A11: validate and consistently link national identifiers; resolve duplicates and legitimate exceptions; make readiness errors block required submissions. Verify manual VNeID claims.
manual: Registration staff checks identity; approve exception rules and obtain authority verification/onboarding access where relevant.
evidence: Identifier validation/duplicate/exception tests; patient-to-record mapping sample; verified identity evidence; missing-ID submission refusal.

requirement: Conform to applicable national technical standards and prescribed medical record content.
how: FHIR R4 resources, terminology, clinical note metadata and Vietnam bundle checks provide a standards-based foundation. [E2,E6]
gap: Map current Vietnamese required forms/fields, standards and workflows. Obtain facility acceptance and validation evidence; FHIR capability alone does not establish Vietnamese EMR conformance.
app: Map required Vietnamese forms/fields/standards against current modules; implement missing fields/workflows or serializers once the approved mapping identifies them. FHIR alone is insufficient.
manual: Clinic approves required record types/forms and licensed workflows; appoints the independent EMR reviewer.
evidence: Current technical/form requirements matrix; complete sample records; conformance test results; facility acceptance.

requirement: Connect to national health databases and the VNeID health book where required.
how: Vietnam adapter exports files; it does not implement an accepted national connection. VNeID identity capture is manual. [E6]
gap: Obtain current interface specifications and credentials, implement required transport/mappings and secure accepted test submissions. National onboarding availability must be checked with the authority.
app: A09: implement current national health/VNeID transport, authentication, mappings, retries, reconciliation and submission audit; validate accepted responses.
manual: Obtain authority specifications, agreements, credentials and test onboarding; establish interface operations.
evidence: Official interface/spec version; onboarding approval; accepted test submission and acknowledgement; retry/reconciliation/error tests.

requirement: Produce current BHYT XML outputs and submit to BHXH when insured services are in scope.
how: health_bhyt creates structured coverage/copay claims. Phase 1 stops before XML transport; report refers to the old Decision 4210 target. [E6]
dates:
QD130 issued 18 Jan 2023;
operational from 1 Jan 2024 [L15]
gap: Use current QD130 amendments and official schema/sample; implement XML, validation, submission and acknowledgements. Tax e-invoicing and FHIR export do not satisfy this requirement.
app: A10: implement current QD130 amended XML, validation and BHXH submission/acknowledgement. Replace historical Decision 4210 assumptions.
manual: Confirm insured-service scope; obtain current schema/sample and BHXH onboarding; finance validates claim mapping.
evidence: Approved current schema and mapping; valid sample XML; accepted BHXH test acknowledgement; coverage/claim reconciliation.

requirement: Complete EMR implementation by the facility-category deadline.
how: EMR spine and exports are installed on master, hhh and template, but signature, national connection and operational evidence gaps remain. [E2,E6,E10]
dates:
Hospitals: 30 Sep 2025
Other qualifying facilities: 31 Dec 2026 [L8]
gap: Confirm the clinic’s licensed category and qualifying care activity. Approve a completion plan and evidence pack for the applicable deadline; installation alone is not readiness.
app: Deliver the applicable clinical tickets and complete acceptance testing; no extra deadline feature is required.
manual: Confirm licensed facility category; approve resources and delivery plan against the applicable rollout deadline; sign readiness acceptance.
evidence: Facility/category evidence; dated plan; completed clinical/control tests; independent acceptance covering all applicable requirements.

requirement: Notify changes and provide version-specific release information on data handling and security.
how: Git versions, module manifests and tenant rollout/release records support traceability and staged upgrades. [E9]
dates:
1 Jan 2026
Contractual notice period to agree [L6]
gap: Publish client release notes and an approved advance-notice process for hosting, sub-processors and material feature changes. Internal logs do not prove delivery to clients.
app: Use existing version/rollout history. No required new release-notes module; produce repeatable data/security change summaries.
manual: Agree and execute client advance notices, release approval and processor/hosting changes; retain proof of delivery.
evidence: Versioned release notes; deployment records; client notices/approvals; data/security impact summary.

requirement: Reassess security after major changes and update impact assessments as required.
how: Rollout tools can identify changed versions and test copies; no signed risk assessment or impact-assessment update receipt establishes compliance. [E9]
dates:
19 Aug 2026 /
1 Jan 2026
Source cites six-month update cycle [L12,L5]
gap: Define change triggers, periodic and urgent dossier updates, reviewers and receipts; counsel to confirm immediate updates versus the six-month cycle.
app: Engineering supplies a version/flow/control diff. No application screen can replace risk reassessment or dossier updates.
manual: Reassess major changes; update impact dossiers under applicable immediate/periodic rules; retain receipts and independent decisions.
evidence: Signed risk reassessment; assessment delta and update receipt; change trigger register; accepted release decision.

requirement: Supplier provides evidence statements for independent clinic verification.
how: This matrix and referenced source files provide an assessment baseline, but are not signed supplier attestations or independent acceptance. [E1–E10]
dates:
Before adoption and each significant change
Client governance requirement
gap: Supplier signs scoped claims and evidence; a clinic-appointed reviewer validates them. Record acceptance, exceptions and next review date separately from implementation.
app: Generate evidence from the exact deployed release; no new app feature required for independent sign-off.
manual: Supplier signs scoped evidence statements; independent clinic reviewer verifies and closes each row or documents a legally valid exception.
evidence: Signed requirement statements; independent acceptance by row; exception basis; owner, date and next review.

requirement: Appoint qualified data-protection personnel through a written decision.
how: User roles can support administration, but a role in software is not a qualified DPO appointment. [E5]
gap: Provide appointment, qualifications, responsibilities and contact details. Check sensitive-health-data implications before relying on any exemption.
app: No code fix appoints or qualifies a DPO; role permissions only support the appointed person.
manual: Clinic appoints qualified privacy personnel in writing, allocates authority/training and confirms applicable exemptions.
evidence: Clinic appointment, education/experience/training and confidentiality files; contact details and assigned duties.

requirement: Prepare and file the clinic’s own processing impact assessment.
how: Data inventory, access, hosting and interface evidence are available inputs; the supplier’s assessment cannot replace the clinic’s. [E1–E10]
dates:
1 Jan 2026
Source: within 60 days of first processing [L5]
gap: Confirm first-processing date and transition treatment; supply dossier and receipt, cross-border assessment where required, and updates.
app: Supply the actual clinic data flow, purpose/access/retention/hosting evidence; no mandatory assessment-filing module.
manual: Clinic prepares/files its own assessment, records first processing/transition treatment, and updates it. Supplier filing does not substitute.
evidence: Clinic assessment and receipt/result as applicable; first-processing record; updates and cross-border dossier where required.

requirement: Issue an internal EMR regulation where electronic medical records are operated.
how: Technical workflows support drafting the rule; no signed clinic policy or staff adoption evidence establishes completion. [E2,E5,E8]
gap: Approve authoring, correction, signing, access, retention, downtime, restore, export and incident procedures with named custodians.
app: Technical changes follow the approved policy; no code fix can issue the clinic regulation.
manual: Director signs and implements internal EMR procedures for access, signing, correction, retention, downtime, restore and export.
evidence: Signed regulation and version; custodian appointment; staff training/acknowledgements; procedure rehearsal.

requirement: Give staff appropriate notices for processing their data and recorded voices.
how: Employee records and recording/transcription features create the relevant processing paths. No issued employee notice is evidenced. [E7]
gap: Map staff data/voice purposes, provide notices and required consent or other lawful basis; retain acknowledgement and withdrawal handling.
app: No mandatory employee-notice module. Adjust recording capture/gates under A01 if a purpose requires permission or acknowledgement.
manual: Issue purpose-specific employee/data/voice notices; establish lawful basis and capture acknowledgement/required consent.
evidence: Issued notice/version and distribution proof; staff acknowledgement or consent; audio purpose/retention register.

requirement: Validate the assumption that the product does not provide clinical decision support.
law: Source assumptions and notes; ND98 as amended
how: Repository includes medication safety checks, NEWS2/telemonitoring alerts and deterioration-risk forecasts, beyond passive CRM/notes. Relevant modules are installed on reviewed systems. [E11,E10]
dates:
ND98: 1 Jan 2022
Before clinical use of in-scope functions [L16]
gap: Obtain an intended-use and regulatory-classification opinion for enabled functions. These features do not automatically establish medical-device status, but the draft’s blanket exclusion cannot be assumed.
app: Inventory enabled decision-support functions; disable excluded functions through supported configuration if needed. Implement any device-specific controls only after classification.
manual: Obtain intended-use/classification opinion; assess registration/quality/clinical validation duties and update the product scope.
evidence: Enabled-feature inventory; signed classification opinion; exclusion configuration/test, or applicable device approval/validation package.
